sections.summary: What the Pinterest Tag is and what it does.

claims.text: The Pinterest Tag is a piece of code you add to your website that lets Pinterest track visitors to your site and the actions they take after seeing your Pinterest ad.

evidence.locator: The Pinterest Tag is a piece of code that you add to your website...

claims.text: Pinterest positions the tag as the way to measure how effective Pinterest ads are, based on the website actions people take after seeing or engaging with an ad.

evidence.locator: Track and optimise conversions; Measure campaign performance; Build audiences for targeting...

sections.summary: How the tag captures visitor and conversion data.

claims.text: The tag works by sending Pinterest data about site visitors and their actions after they saw or engaged with a Pinterest ad.

evidence.locator: If you add the Pinterest tag to your website, you'll be able to: Track and optimise conversions...

claims.text: Event-level tracking implies additional event code on key pages; Pinterest points to a separate base-code article for manual setup but does not describe event-code details.

evidence.locator: What's next? If you've chosen to use manual setup, learn how to add the base code.

claims.text: Pinterest offers the Conversions API to use in addition to the tag to maximise visibility into conversions.

evidence.locator: You also have the option to use the Pinterest Conversions API in addition to the Pinterest tag...

sections.summary: When the tag is the right tool, and when not.

claims.text: Use it when you want to track and optimise conversions from Pinterest ads.

evidence.locator: Track and optimise conversions

claims.text: Use it when you need to measure campaign performance or build audiences for targeting.

evidence.locator: Measure campaign performance; Build audiences for targeting

claims.text: Do not rely on it when you need server-side or cross-platform conversion visibility — the tag is browser-based, which is why Pinterest offers the Conversions API as a supplement to maximise conversion visibility.

evidence.locator: This means you can measure how effective your Pinterest ads are...

sections.summary: How to install the tag, per Pinterest's documented steps.

claims.text: First, get a Pinterest business account.

evidence.locator: Before you can add the Pinterest Tag to your website, you need to: Get a Pinterest business account; Create an advertiser account
Create an advertiser account

claims.text: Third, log in to your Pinterest business account, open the collapsed menu in the top left, and under Business click Conversions.

evidence.locator: Log in to your Pinterest business account... Under Business, click Conversions

claims.text: Fourth, click Get started and choose one of three installation methods: an integration partner, emailing instructions to a developer or colleague, or manual setup.

evidence.locator: Click Get started. Choose how you'd like to install the Pinterest Tag

claims.text: Fifth, for an integration partner: paste your website URL, click Check, and if eligible select a partner to view instructions.

evidence.locator: Use an integration partner: Paste your website URL... then click Check

claims.text: Sixth, alternatively click Email instruction to send steps to someone, or click Skip to proceed with manual setup yourself.

evidence.locator: Email instructions: Click Email instruction... Use manual setup: Click Skip

claims.text: Seventh, install from desktop; Pinterest states installation currently requires a desktop device.

evidence.locator: At the moment, you'll need to use your desktop to install the Pinterest Tag

claims.text: Manual setup continues in a separate article on adding the base code; those specific steps are not covered by Pinterest's documentation.

evidence.locator: What's next? If you've chosen to use manual setup, learn how to add the base code.

sections.summary: What to monitor once the tag is live; Pinterest gives no vendor uplift figures.

claims.text: A practical early indicator is that the tag appears in Ads Manager — but expect up to 24 hours after installation before it does; expect nothing meaningful before the tag is reflected.

evidence.locator: After you've installed the Pinterest Tag, it can take up to 24 hours to be reflected in Ads Manager.

claims.text: Once tracking is live, use conversion actions as your primary metric, since the tag's documented purpose is measuring on-site actions after ad exposure; treat reported conversions as attributed measurements, not proof of incremental lift, and weigh the trade-off that browser-based tracking may miss conversions the Conversions API would capture.

evidence.locator: Track and optimise conversions; Measure campaign performance; Access Conversion Insights

relationships.name: Enhanced conversions for web
relationships.difference: The Pinterest Tag is Pinterest's on-site tracking code for measuring Pinterest ad performance; Enhanced conversions for web is a Google Ads feature that sends hashed first-party user-provided data at conversion time to improve online conversion measurement via signed-in account matching — a measurement-enhancement mechanism, not a site-wide tracking tag, and it belongs to a different ad platform.
relationships.context: Website conversion tracking for Pinterest advertisers vs browser-event tracking for Google Ads advertisers

evidence.locator: * [About enhanced conversions](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/9888656)

relationships.name: First-party cookies with Events API
relationships.difference: The Events API first-party cookie (ttp) stores unique identifiers limited to the advertiser's domain and is shared with the TikTok Events API alongside the Pixel; the Pinterest Tag is Pinterest's own on-site code. Pinterest's documentation recommends its own Conversions API alongside the tag, but the TikTok cookie/API setup is platform-specific to TikTok and not interchangeable.
relationships.context: Choosing between tag-only and tag-plus-server-event tracking on Pinterest

evidence.locator: "1st Party Cookie (if using with Pixel): Unique identifiers saved in the ttp first-party cookie and limited to the advertiser's domain"
